title: Admin portal roles, users and content permissions: system and custom roles, resource categories, RBAC and ABAC, and the scope of content permissions

prose.label: System roles.
prose.text: {{system-roles-fixed}} {{system-roles-per-app}} The role names and matrices are open {{gap:system-role-list}}.

prose.label: Roles page actions.
prose.text: {{roles-page-actions}} System roles cannot be modified {{system-roles-fixed|ref}} and the Admin role cannot be duplicated {{custom-role-permissions|ref}}.

prose.label: Resource categories.
prose.text: {{resources-platform}} {{resources-explore}} {{resources-uvm}} {{resources-aem}} {{resources-agentic-soc}} The categories do not cover Identity Protection or automation {{gap:resource-categories-coverage}}.

prose.label: Users.
prose.text: {{user-access-model}} {{user-default-no-access}} What deactivating and deleting a user do is open {{gap:deactivate-delete-scope}}.

system-roles-fixed.statement: System roles are predefined, cannot be modified, and are updated automatically when new features are introduced, while permissions for new features must be added manually to custom roles.

quotes: System roles are predefined by the Agentic SecOps Platform and cannot be modified.
These roles are maintained by the system and are updated automatically when new features are introduced.
When new system features are introduced, related permissions must be manually added to custom roles.

system-roles-per-app.statement: The set of system roles differs between UVM, AEM and Agentic SOC, and a role's permissions are seen by clicking the role name on the Roles page to open its matrix.

quotes: The set of available system roles differs between Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM), Asset Exposure Management (AEM), and Agentic SOC
To view the specific permissions assigned to a role, click the role name on the Roles page.
This opens the role's matrix, where you can view the detailed actions the role can perform.

custom-role-permissions.statement: Custom roles grant Read, Create, Edit, Delete and Audit permissions per resource, selecting a higher-level permission such as Edit enables the required lower-level ones such as Read, and the system Admin role cannot be duplicated.

quotes: you can select permissions (i.e., Read, Create, Edit, Delete, and Audit) for custom roles to control access and operations on those resources.
Selecting a higher-level permission (e.g., Edit) automatically enables required lower-level permissions (e.g., Read).
You can't duplicate the system Admin role.

roles-page-actions.statement: The Roles page in the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform) gives a centralized view of all system and custom roles, and the page lists the actions Edit Users in the Role, Duplicate a Role, Edit a Custom Role and Delete a Role.

quotes: You can manage and monitor roles from the Roles page in the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform)
where you'll find a centralized view of all configured system roles and custom roles in your account
Edit Users in the Role
Duplicate a Role
Edit a Custom Role
Delete a Role

resources-platform.statement: The Platform resource category of a custom role covers Model Management, Data Source Mapping, Data Source, User Saved Views, Outegrations and Authentications.

quotes: | Model Management | Manage data model entities and their fields |
| Data Source Mapping | View and manage data source mapping |
| Data Source | View, create, and manage data sources |
| User Saved Views | View, create, and manage user-saved views across the Agentic SecOps Platform |
| Outegrations | View and manage outegrations |
| Authentications | View and manage authentications |

resources-explore.statement: The Explore category's table of key analytics resources has Search (view and search logs) and Reports & Dashboards (view and manage custom dashboards and reports).

quotes: | Search | View and search logs |
| Reports & Dashboards | View and manage custom dashboards and reports |
The following table outlines key analytics resources and the specific types of access that can be granted to users through custom roles:

resources-uvm.statement: The Vulnerabilities App category (UVM) lists Dashboards & Analytics, Tickets Page, Tickets Settings, Findings Page, Assets Page, Exceptions Page and Exceptions Settings; ticket settings cover scoring, grouping rules and life-cycle customization and exception settings cover the form, assignment rules and notifications.

quotes: | Dashboards & Analytics | Built-in vulnerability dashboard and analytics |
| Tickets Page | View and manage tickets |
| Tickets Settings | Ticket scoring, grouping rules, and life-cycle customization |
| Findings Page | View and manage findings |
| Exceptions Page | View and manage exceptions |
| Exceptions Settings | Exceptions form, assignment rules, and notification customization |
| Assets Page | View and manage assets |

resources-aem.statement: The Assets App category (AEM) lists Violations Tickets, Policy Violations, Policy Violations Outegrations, Policy Rule, Analytics & Insights, Assets Page and Asset Outegrations.

quotes: | Violations Tickets | View and manage policy violations |
| Policy Violations | Violation ticket grouping rules and life-cycle customization |
| Policy Violations Outegrations | Trigger third-party outegrations from policy violations |
| Policy Rule | View and manage policy rules |
| Analytics & Insights | Built-in vulnerability dashboard and analytics |
| Asset Outegrations | Trigger third-party outegrations from assets |
| Assets Page | View and manage assets |

resources-agentic-soc.statement: The Agentic SOC category lists Dashboards & Analytics, Incidents Page, Incident Settings and Alerts Page.

quotes: | Dashboards & Analytics | View and manage built-in Agentic SOC dashboards and analytics |
| Incidents Page | View and manage incidents |
| Incident Settings | Incident scoring, grouping rules, and life-cycle customization |
| Alerts Page | View and manage alerts |

role-timing-immediate.statement: The custom role page says the selected users' roles are updated immediately.

quotes: The selected users' roles are updated immediately.
Click Finish.

role-timing-refresh.statement: The Managing User Roles page says assigned roles are applied on the user's next browser refresh.

quotes: Assigned roles are applied on the user's next browser refresh.

user-default-no-access.statement: A new user without a selected role gets the default No Access role, and removing a user's role without assigning another leaves the default role, which grants no permissions but keeps the user's access to the system.

quotes: If you don't, the user is assigned the default No Access role.
When removing a user's role without assigning them a new role, the user is automatically assigned the default role.
While the default role grants no permissions within the account, it preserves the user's access to the system

user-access-model.statement: Users are given RBAC roles and optionally ABAC permissions, and can be deactivated or deleted; the Create User page asks for email, first and last name, an optional default (main) account and a role.

quotes: assigning Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), optionally assigning Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) permissions, and deactivating or deleting users
Main Account: (Optional) If you have more than one account, set the user's default account.
Deactivate Users
Delete Users
Email: Enter the user's organization email.
First Name: Enter the user's first name.
Last Name: Enter the user's last name.
Roles: Expand the section and select a role for the user.

content-permission-purpose.statement: Role permissions control the actions a user can perform, while content permissions limit the data the user can view and act on; assignments take effect on the user's next browser refresh.

quotes: While role permissions dictate the actions the user can perform (e.g., create a dashboard, merge tickets), content permissions limit the scope of data the user can view and is authorized to perform those actions on.
When assigned, access changes take effect on the user's next browser refresh.

content-permission-scope.statement: Content permissions apply only to an account's mapped data, so they do not restrict unmapped data such as Logs or Data Mapping access granted by a role.

quotes: Content permissions only apply to an account's mapped data, so they won't restrict access to unmapped data across the Agentic Security Operations Platform
if a user's role grants them access to Logs or Data Mapping, their content permissions won't apply to those resources.

content-permission-scheduled-exports.statement: Content restrictions on scheduled reports and custom dashboard exports follow the permission set of the user who created the report or dashboard, not the receiver, so a delivered report can include data the receiver could not access directly.

quotes: content restrictions for scheduled reports and custom dashboard exports conform to the permission set of the user that created the report or the dashboard.
The permission set of the receiver is not considered, so the delivered report can include data that the receiver can't access by their own permissions if they are also a user in the system.

content-permission-conditions.statement: A content permission set's filter conditions pick a field, an operator and a value, and are combined with AND (applies only if all conditions are met) or OR (applies if any condition is met).

evidence.after: Conditions define the data included in the permission set (i.e., what data should be included in the user's access).
quotes: Select an operator (e.g., Equals, Contains). Available operators vary depending on the selected field type.
AND applies the content permissions to users only if all conditions in the rule are met.
OR applies the content permissions to users if any of the conditions in the rule are met.
Select a field that the condition should be based on.
Enter the value that the rule should apply to.

content-permission-dynamic.statement: A dynamic condition grants access based on the current user's email address using the {user_email} value (the example uses the Assignee Email field), and only the Equals operator is supported.

quotes: add a condition to the Linux Team permission set, select the Assignee Email field, and enter the dynamic {user_email} value.
Only the Equals operator is supported, as the field's value should be a unique identifier.
You can grant dynamic access based on the email address of the current user to avoid the need to create a separate condition for each individual user email address.

content-permission-manual-override.statement: With manual content validation, content permissions can restrict which values users may pick when manually updating a field, for example letting security analysts choose Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive or Suspicious on an incident Verdict while reserving Malicious and True Positive for senior security analysts or incident responders.

quotes: such as Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious, or True Positive
you can create a content permission set that only allows security analysts to select Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, or Suspicious.
manual updates for high-impact values (e.g., Malicious and True Positive) are only available to certain users
You can then create another content permission set that only allows senior security analysts or incident responders to select all values.
you can allow users to manually update the Verdict field of an Agentic SOC incident.
With manual content validation, you can define the approved values users can enter

content-permission-assign.statement: Content permissions can be assigned only after a user is created and saved; removing a permission set removes the access limit it set, so the user is no longer limited to the data it defined.

quotes: Content permissions can only be assigned after a user is created and saved.
Removing content permission sets from users removes their access limit from the defined data.

role-update-timing.summary: The Creating Custom Roles page says the selected users' roles are updated immediately, while the Managing User Roles page says assigned roles are applied on the user's next browser refresh.

positions.says: The selected users' roles are updated immediately.

quotes: The selected users' roles are updated immediately.

positions.says: Assigned roles are applied on the user's next browser refresh.

quotes: Assigned roles are applied on the user's next browser refresh.

role-update-timing.impact: Whether a user sees a new role without refreshing the browser depends on which page is right; the content-permission pages also say changes apply on the next browser refresh.

resource-categories-coverage.title: Which role resources govern Identity Protection and automation
resource-categories-coverage.detail: The system-role and custom-role tables quoted here list the Platform, Explore, Vulnerabilities, Assets and Agentic SOC categories only; they show no Identity Protection or playbook and automation-rule resources, although those areas exist on other captured pages (Identities, Automations). The role pages do not say whether other resources cover them.

system-role-list.title: Which system roles exist for UVM, AEM and Agentic SOC and what they permit
system-role-list.detail: The Understanding System Roles capture ends at the headings UVM, AEM and Agentic SOC with no role names or permission matrices, and the Managing System & Custom Roles page only lists four actions (Edit Users in the Role, Duplicate a Role, Edit a Custom Role, Delete a Role).

deactivate-delete-scope.title: What deactivating and deleting a user do
deactivate-delete-scope.detail: The Creating & Managing Users page lists Deactivate Users and Delete Users as actions without describing their scope or effect.
